item.title: Gravity Forms Path Traversal → Arbitrary File Deletion (CVE-2026-48866)
item.description:

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System Gravity Forms plugin for WordPress
Versions Affected <= 2.10.0.1 (fixed in 2.10.1)

Authentication Required No for injection (unauthenticated form submission); admin interaction/credentials required to trigger the actual file deletion
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

Gravity Forms stores the URL of uploaded files in a form entry via the gform_uploaded_files parameter without stripping ../ sequences (esc_url_raw() and is_valid_url() both accept path-traversal payloads). When an entry containing such a URL is later deleted — typically by an admin doing routine cleanup — get_physical_file_path() converts the URL to a filesystem path via str_replace(), which preserves the ../ sequences, and the resulting path is passed to unlink() with no validation. This lets an unauthenticated attacker plant a poisoned entry that deletes an arbitrary file (e.g. wp-config.php, .htaccess, a WAF plugin file) once the entry is removed. The included PoC (poc.py) automates both the injection phase and, given admin credentials, the trigger phase, then checks whether the target file’s removal knocked the site offline.
